messages:
ajay: quick heads-up — I’m seeing a performance regression on the continuous batching path when prefix cache hit rate > ~60%. Batch formation skews toward tiny batches of cached requests, increasing per-token overhead. profiling attached.

maria: ugh. is this the packing policy that prefers cache_hits first? @ajay any logs/snippets? :eyes:

ajay: yeah. repro on staging with simulated traffic. key bits: queue policy = FIFO with pack_by_cache_hit=true, token_budget_target=2048. when a flow of cached prefixes arrives they get packed tightly but they have near-zero decode cost; they block non-cached requests from filling large token budgets.

leo: can you paste the profiler flame or top metrics? curious about kernel selection churn too — tiny batches might force different kernel paths.

ajay: pasted below — focus on tail because kernels keep switching.

```
# simplified perf snapshot (staging run)
requests_total: 1200
cache_hit_rate: 0.64
avg_batch_size_tokens: 18
p95_latency_token_ms: 12.4
kernel_switches_per_minute: 42  # up from 9 baseline
kv_cache_lookup_ms_avg: 0.3
batch_formation_delay_ms_avg: 6.2
```

ajay: note kernel_switches_per_minute correlates with tiny batches and different quant/path chosen by kernel selector. switching penalty explains p95 rise.

tara: interesting — so cached prefixes are both cheap to serve but harmful for batching. two obvious levers: (1) change queue policy to prefer fill-by-cost (estimate decode cost) instead of cache_hit, (2) add a small hold window for cached requests to let non-cached ones join.

maria: for (1) we could estimate cost = max(1, tokens_to_generate - cached_prefix_tokens) * token_cost_weight and pack by that. For (2) what window are we thinking? 2-10 ms?

leo: quick sim I ran: using hold_window=8ms and pack_by_estimated_cost reduces kernel switches by ~70% and raises avg_batch_size_tokens to ~64, overall token throughput improved. downside: a tiny extra latency for pure cached hits (~+4ms median).

ajay: sim looks promising. also we should avoid starving cached traffic — they often come from high-qps clients. propose: adaptive hold_window proportional to current queue depth and recent cache hit ratio: hold = clamp(ceil( (1 - hit_rate) * 12 ), 2, 20) ms.

maria: +1 on adaptive approach. should also surface a metric: split batch composition (cached_tokens vs uncached_tokens) and kernel_switch_rate. add an alert if kernel_switch_rate > 20/min and p95 latency regresses.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for branch cache/prefetch-pack-tune (build 8852).

ajay: next steps: 1) add pack_by_estimated_cost flag + adaptive hold_window; 2) instrument batch composition metrics; 3) run canary with traffic replay and kernel-switch monitor. I'll open a PR with configs and sim results.

tara: if you can drop the PR link here I’ll review. also add a small unit test for the cost estimator so we don’t regress weighting.

ajay: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412 (draft) — includes sim harness and a short note on fallback: if throughput drops for uncached heavy clients then we fallback to strict FIFO.

maria: nice. also log an incident ticket so support can watch affected customers during canary.

leo: one more thought — kernel selector should be tolerant to small batches: add hysteresis so it doesn’t switch for transient changes. I'll sketch a change after PR review.

ajay: will add a TODO in the PR for kernel selector hysteresis. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
